definition: The task of identifying inputs that differ significantly from the distribution of data a model was trained on, so the system can flag uncertainty or defer to a human.
details: OOD detection is important for safe deployment, helping systems recognize when they are being asked to operate outside their reliable competence and should respond with caution or abstain.
story: Picture a parachute packed by a second pair of hands: nobody plans to need it, but everyone is glad it was checked. The idea is simple: before something powerful is let loose, someone checks that it will not do real harm to real people. It is the habit of asking, before every launch, what could go wrong — and then doing something about it. Caution is not the enemy of progress — it is the reason progress gets to keep going. That deliberate caution is Out-of-Distribution Detection.
